correctness.rationale: The graph is defined independently of any graph-library labeling as thirty-six cyclically stable five-sets of twelve, joined by disjointness. The included standard-library verifier exhaustively enumerates 1,519,600 augmented simplices, reconstructs 759,796 disjoint Morse pairs, checks six critical dimension-six and two critical dimension-eight simplices and tests every one of 12,264,696 directed Hasse incidences by complete Kahn topological sorting. Its independent deletion–closed-neighborhood polynomial recursion reproduces all face counts. Forman’s theorem yields a CW model with a point, six six-cells and two eight-cells. Every integral cellular differential vanishes by dimension, giving the claimed torsion-free reduced integral homology. Five-connectivity follows from the CW skeleton. No unverified unstable attaching map or infinite extension is asserted.

originality.rationale: Braun arXiv:0912.0720v1 is a direct primary inspection of SG(n,2) and explicitly leaves its independence-complex homotopy unknown while solving SG(2,k) and distinct E(2n+2). Braun and Zeckner arXiv:1102.1984v1 calculate neighborhood complexes, which are not independence complexes. A published result for SG(4,2) on twenty-five vertices and another for SG(2,k) do not cover the thirty-six-vertex SG(5,2) homology. Feng-Wang 2024 concerns ordinary Kneser graphs, not this stable induced subgraph. Exact parameter, alias, numeric and broader coverage searches found no covering record. Residual bibliographic incompleteness is acknowledged.
residual_risks: An unindexed or inaccessible later calculation for the exact SG(5,2) complex might exist; available search results cannot certify universal priority.

value.rationale: The integral homology of SG(n,2) is a motivated historical gap identified by Braun, not a contrived graph slice. This 36-vertex n=5 case is a natural next higher-rank stable Kneser test and exhibits a mixed-degree (six/eight) torsion-free homology profile and 8-cell reduced CW model, invisible to generic neighborhood-complex sphere theorems or the previously determined n=4 homotopy example. It provides concrete constraints for understanding nonconcentration, higher-cell attaching maps, and possible parameter patterns, without a false general or wedge claim.
